I make beer regularly and I've also made some mead. It's true that mead is much simpler, but beer really isn't that much tougher, especially if you start with extract kits. Here are some tips/suggestions, in no particular order:

  • Sanitizing is the most important thing, but don't freak out about it. You don't want to risk ruining a batch, but if you slip up, there's no point in ruining the batch over the possibility of a problem. Keep going, be careful about the rest of your sanitizing, and everything will likely work out.
  • Follow a recipe, at least when you're starting out. If you mix honey and water then add yeast, you'll get mead, but it might not be all that good. Take advantage of the work others have already done.
  • Boil (or otherwise sanitize) the water before adding the honey. You don't want or need to boil honey.
  • When you've used up the sanitizer you have, I strongly recommend StarSan. It's awesome.
  • Put either sanitizer (if it's safe, I'm not sure about the one you're using) or alcohol in your airlock. If barometric pressure rises, sometimes the fluid in the airlock gets sucked into your fermentor, and plain water has a risk of carrying bacteria with it. As an alternative, consider a blow-off tube.
  • Use a swamp cooler. Yeast generally prefer temperatures cooler than room temperature. A simple way to accomplish this is by putting your fermentor in a tub with a little water in it, and draping a towel or old shirt over the fermentor. The water soaks into the cloth, then evaporates, cooling the fermentor.
  • Champagne yeast is fine for starting with, but isn't always the best choice. Being able to reach a high ABV isn't usually as important as using a yeast that provides the flavors (or lack thereof) you're looking for. That said, it is a good choice if you intend to make a particularly strong mead.
  • Be patient. Even when primary fermentation is finished, the yeast are still cleaning up after themselves. Don't bother checking your results until you're pretty sure it's done. Every time you mess with it you have a chance of introducing bacteria. To be sure it's done, you need to either measure the specific gravity and get the same result several days in a row, or just give it way longer than you think it needs.
  • Speaking of SG, if you want to know your ABV, you need to measure your SG before and after fermenting. This means getting either a hydrometer or a refractometer. If you decide to use a hydrometer, get at least two; they break easily.
  • Keep a log of everything you do. This will help you when making future batches.
  • Unless you filter your mead/wine/beer, it will continue to condition while in the bottle. So if you open one bottle, and aren't that happy with the results, give the others another week or two before trying again. You might find it much improved.
  • FWIW, I used store-bought honey and was perfectly happy with the results. I think you'd have to be quite experienced with mead before you'd notice the difference between sources of honey, but that's your call.
  • Relax, Don't Worry, Have a Homebrew.

Well, that's all that comes to mind right now. Good luck!
